headline: GOLIATH RESOURCES: 74.67 g/t GOLD OVER 1.1m — SUREBET BONANZA ZONE EXPANDS 540m, BC GOLDEN TRIANGLE
snippet: Goliath Resources reported August 6, 2026 initial 2026 drill results from its Golddigger property in BC's Golden Triangle, with highlight hole GD-26-418 returning 8.09 g/t AuEq over 16.00 metres from the Surebet Zone — including a 74.67 g/t AuEq hit over 1.10 metres and a separate 4.42 g/t AuEq over 5.00 metres in the Bonanza Zone from the same hole. The Bonanza Zone has now expanded by 540 metres to the southwest, 100 metres to the north, and 100 metres to the west — expanding in three independent directions simultaneously, the geological signature of a large-scale structurally controlled gold system rather than a narrow vein. The adjacent Golden Gate Zone now measures approximately 1.6 kilometres east-west by 1.5 kilometres north-south and remains open on all sides. Goliath has completed 35 of 98 planned holes (approximately 20,000 metres of a fully-funded 50,000-metre program) using seven active drill rigs — meaning the discovery has yielded its strongest results in the first third of drilling, with the growth of the system still underway. For junior mining investors, the key signal is that high-grade grades are appearing not just in narrow intervals but over meaningful widths within a system now measured in hundreds of metres of spatial extent — the geometry that supports both underground and open-pit development scenarios. At $4,300+ gold, every tonne at these grades in a Tier 1 Canadian jurisdiction is materially more valuable than it was 18 months ago.

headline: TUDOR GOLD TUD.V: DUAL DISCOVERY AT TREATY CREEK — NEW COPPER-GOLD PORPHYRY AND EPITHERMAL BOTH CONFIRMED IN ONE DRILL PROGRAM
snippet: Tudor Gold Corp. (TSXV: TUD) reported August 6, 2026 that results from the first four holes of its 2026 Treaty Creek exploration program have confirmed two entirely new mineral systems within the Perfectstorm Zone — both representing material additions to one of Canada's largest undeveloped gold districts. The PSP Zone (Perfectstorm Porphyry) delivered 82.90 metres grading 0.24 g/t gold, 2.11 g/t silver, 0.21% copper, and 50.76 ppm molybdenum in hole PS-26-15, and 67.35 metres at 0.34 g/t gold, 1.89 g/t silver, and 0.27% copper in hole PS-26-18 — a bulk-tonnage copper-gold-moly porphyry intercept sitting approximately one kilometre from Treaty Creek's flagship Goldstorm Deposit. The PSE Zone (Perfectstorm Epithermal) represents a higher-grade gold-silver mineralization style within the same area, complementing the porphyry shell and suggesting the mineralizing system has both a low-grade bulk-tonnage envelope and higher-grade epithermal interior — the geological architecture that has historically produced the largest gold-copper discoveries in the Golden Triangle, including Seabridge's KSM and Newcrest's Brucejack. Tudor's 80%-owned Treaty Creek is located in NW British Columbia between two of BC's most advanced large-scale mining projects, placing any discovery in a district already proving logistically viable for development-scale operations.

headline: IAMGOLD Q2: $507M EBITDA, 188K OZ — CÔTÉ GOLD HITS FULL CAPACITY; MINE-SITE FREE CASH FLOW $369M
snippet: IAMGOLD Corporation (TSX: IMG, NYSE: IAG) reported August 6, 2026 second-quarter 2026 results that mark the company's strongest operational performance since the commissioning of the Côté Gold Mine in Ontario — its flagship new asset and one of the largest new gold mines opened in North America in a decade. Consolidated gold production was 188,100 ounces with 195,100 ounces sold at an average realized gold price of $4,384 per ounce, generating revenue of $856.9 million and adjusted EBITDA of $507.3 million. Mine-site free cash flow of $368.9 million was among IAMGOLD's highest on record. The Côté Gold operational update was the centrepiece of the report: the replacement of a conveyor belt in May and the commissioning of a second cone crusher allowed the plant to operate at near-full processing capacity in June, removing the production ramp constraints that had been the primary investor concern since the mine entered commercial production. Management indicated that contracted crushing is now behind the company, and they expect production to increase and unit costs to decline through the second half of 2026 as throughput rates stabilize at design capacity. Net earnings for the quarter reached $230.5 million ($0.40 per share). For investors tracking Côté Gold as a case study in new-mine commissioning at a time of record gold prices, the Q2 results confirm that the ramp-up execution risk is largely resolved, converting what had been a development story into a cash-flow machine.

headline: TOREX GOLD Q2: $94M FREE CASH FLOW, $406M REVENUE — MEDIA LUNA UNDERGROUND RAMP ON TRACK IN MEXICO (TXG)
snippet: Torex Gold Resources Inc. (TSX: TXG) reported August 6, 2026 strong second-quarter 2026 results, delivering net income of $113.8 million, revenue of $406.9 million, adjusted EBITDA of $203.5 million, and free cash flow of $94.2 million — one of the company's best financial quarters on record and one achieved simultaneously with the ongoing ramp-up of the Media Luna underground mine at its Morelos Complex in Guerrero State, Mexico. Media Luna, a significant capital expansion project that has extended the mine life of the Morelos Complex beyond 2030, reached a production milestone in Q2 as underground mining from the new Media Luna zones began contributing meaningful gold ounces alongside the existing El Limón Guajes open-pit operations. The combination of open-pit and underground production streams at a single Guerrero State operation has lowered Torex's unit cost structure on a per-ounce basis, widening margins at a time when gold's realized price is near all-time highs. For retail investors monitoring mid-tier gold producers that are generating genuine free cash flow — not just adjusted numbers — Torex represents a company that has successfully executed a major underground expansion while maintaining production and accumulating cash. The Mexico jurisdiction risk is a persistent investor concern, but Torex's long operating track record in Guerrero and a community relations framework built over 15 years of operations have kept Morelos politically stable through successive changes in Mexican government.

headline: GALIANO GOLD Q2: ASANKO MINE EBITDA $105.6M, NET INCOME $0.24/SHARE — GHANA PRODUCTION BEATS ESTIMATES (GAU)
snippet: Galiano Gold Inc. (TSX/NYSE: GAU) reported August 6, 2026 second-quarter 2026 results reflecting strong performance at its flagship Asanko Gold Mine in Ghana, with EBITDA of $105.6 million, adjusted EBITDA of $78.5 million, and net income of $0.24 per basic share. The West African production beat is notable for two reasons: Ghana is one of Africa's most politically stable mining jurisdictions, and Galiano has operated Asanko — formerly the Obuasi regional complex — through a series of mine expansions and grade variability cycles that have tested management discipline. Delivering $105.6 million in EBITDA at a West African open-pit mine in a single quarter reflects both the current gold price environment and Galiano's operational progress in increasing recovered grade from the Abore and Esaase pits. For retail investors in the junior-to-mid-tier space, Galiano occupies an interesting position: it is large enough to generate institutional-quality quarterly cash flows but still trades at valuations that reflect its smaller market capitalization relative to senior producers, creating the type of NAV discount that BofA and other bank analysts have identified as the primary opportunity in gold mining equities at current gold prices. The Q2 results reinforce a narrative of operational stability that is required before junior-to-mid-tier miners can command tighter NAV discounts.

headline: ANGLOGOLD ASHANTI Q2: EBITDA +46% TO $2B, $2 BILLION BUYBACK APPROVED — BIGGEST SHAREHOLDER RETURN IN COMPANY HISTORY
snippet: AngloGold Ashanti plc (NYSE: AU, JSE: ANG) reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $2.0 billion — a 46% year-on-year increase — and announced that shareholders formally approved a US$2.0 billion share repurchase programme on July 23, 2026, representing the largest buyback in the company's history. The programme awaits South African Reserve Bank (SARB) approval before execution commences, but its approval by shareholders signals that AngloGold's board has concluded that, at the current gold price, returning capital via buybacks is more value-accretive than retaining cash for acquisitions. H1 2026 dividends totalled US$1.88 per share ($1.16 in Q1 + $0.72 in Q2), representing approximately US$949 million returned to shareholders in dividends alone — before the buyback begins. Free cash flow in Q2 rose 36% to $727 million. The significance of the AngloGold results for junior mining investors extends beyond the individual company: as one of the world's three largest gold producers by output, AngloGold's capital return framework sets a market benchmark for what is possible in gold mining at $4,000+ gold. When majors begin buying back $2 billion of their own shares, the signal to the market is that the cycle is real, margins are wide, and the gold price is not about to revert to historical averages — a macro confirmation that supports the rerating thesis for junior developers at even wider NAV discounts to the majors that are generating the capital returns.

headline: ABITIBI METALS B26 QUEBEC: 3.63% CU OVER 14m AT 946m DEPTH + NEW ZINC-SILVER ZONE 1.5KM FROM DEPOSIT (CSE: AMQ)
snippet: Abitibi Metals Corp. (CSE: AMQ, OTC: AMQFF), which is backed by Discovery Silver and focused on its 100%-owned B26 polymetallic project in northwestern Quebec, reported August 5, 2026 two distinct positive developments at the same asset: a new high-grade copper intercept within the main B26 horizon — 46.7 metres grading 1.33% copper, 0.13 g/t gold, and 3.39 g/t silver from 946 metres depth, including 14 metres at 3.63% copper, 0.37 g/t gold, and 7.67 g/t silver — and the discovery of a new potential volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) zinc-silver mineralised zone approximately 1.5 kilometres west of the B26 Deposit. The copper intercept at 946 metres depth confirms that B26's high-grade core continues to improve with depth rather than deteriorating, a pattern consistent with the geometry of deep VMS deposits that become more massive (and hence higher grade) as drill depth increases toward the feeder zone. The new zinc-silver zone 1.5 kilometres to the west represents a completely separate target — and in VMS geology, a satellite zone at this proximity to a known deposit often represents a complementary lens of the same mineralising event at a different point along the hydrothermal corridor. B26 is located approximately 90 km west of Matagami in one of Canada's most prolific base metal districts. Abitibi completed its buyout of the remaining 20% SOQUEM interest in June, making the asset fully owned heading into a resource expansion phase.

headline: NEXMETALS SELKIRK BOTSWANA: NI 43-101 FILED, 1.1B LB CuEq INDICATED — RESOURCE UP 63%, ADDS COBALT AND PGEs (NEXM)
snippet: NexMetals Mining Corp. (TSXV: NEXM) filed an independent NI 43-101 technical report on August 7, 2026 supporting the 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate for its Selkirk Project in Botswana — a past-producing copper-nickel-platinum group elements (PGE) deposit located approximately 75 kilometres northeast of the company's flagship Selebi Project. The 2026 MRE, originally announced June 24, outlines an Indicated Mineral Resource of 78.2 million tonnes grading 0.66% copper equivalent, containing approximately 1.1 billion pounds of CuEq, plus an Inferred Resource of 15.1 million tonnes grading 0.60% CuEq containing approximately 200 million pounds — a total of 1.3 billion pounds of CuEq across both categories. The resource increased by approximately 63% from the previous estimate, driven by: improved metallurgical recoveries, the addition of cobalt, silver, and gold as newly designated payable metals (which were previously excluded from the CuEq calculation), and an expanded mineralized envelope supported by re-assaying and twin drilling completed in 2025. The NI 43-101 filing, rather than the original announcement, is the document that allows institutional investors and analysts to apply standard resource classification to the deposit and begin economic modelling — making this filing the trigger for formal analyst coverage initiation. Botswana is sub-Saharan Africa's most mining-friendly jurisdiction and a Tier 2 address for critical minerals investors looking for copper at lower sovereign risk than the DRC or Zambia.

headline: BARRICK MINING Q2 RESULTS MONDAY AUG 10 — FIRST MAJOR GOLD CO REPORTING AT $4,300+ GOLD; BRISTOW SETS SECTOR TONE
snippet: Barrick Mining Corporation (TSX: ABX, NYSE: GOLD) is scheduled to release second-quarter 2026 results before the opening bell on Monday August 10 — the first of the three largest gold companies to report Q2 results, and the most anticipated since Barrick's Q2 2026 represents the first full quarter in the company's history where gold averaged above $4,000 per ounce throughout the entire reporting period. Analysts are watching for four key data points beyond the headline production figure: (1) whether Barrick can deliver the cost improvement at Kibali and Lumwana that management guided toward for H2 2026; (2) any update on the Reko Diq copper-gold project in Pakistan, where construction financing and host-country economics are under active negotiation; (3) capital return commentary, including whether Barrick will announce a buyback programme to compete with AngloGold Ashanti's newly approved $2.0 billion programme; and (4) any revision to the five-year production profile, which has been closely watched since Barrick's Nevada and Africa operations experienced grade variability in 2025. CEO Mark Bristow's quarterly call is typically one of the most widely followed conversations in the gold sector, particularly for its macro commentary on gold price sustainability, central bank demand, and the state of global deal-making. The call timing on Monday August 10 arrives 48 hours before July CPI data (August 12) and immediately before Franco-Nevada Q2 results (August 11), making it the first piece of a three-event sequence that will define sentiment for gold investors through mid-August.

headline: COT AUG 7: GOLD SPECS ADD 15K NET LONGS, SILVER AT 9K — BOTH FAR BELOW CYCLE PEAKS; POSITIONING LEAVES ROOM TO RUN
snippet: The CFTC Commitments of Traders (COT) report released Friday August 7, covering positions as of July 28, 2026, shows a precious metals positioning picture that is bullish for the sector: not because speculators are heavily long — they are not — but because their current positioning leaves substantial room for additional buying as the gold and silver breakout matures. Gold speculative net positions rose to 197,600 contracts (from 182,100 the prior week), adding approximately 15,000 contracts as the NFP miss on August 7 catalysed the largest single-session gold rally in months. Managed money in silver is net long only 9,182 COMEX contracts — a level that represents a fraction of the speculative commitment seen at the peaks of prior silver bull runs, when managed money positions reached 70,000–90,000 contracts. The contrast between gold (where speculative longs are rebuilding from a depressed base following the multi-month correction) and silver (where positioning is near a structural floor despite the metal's breakout above $64) is the most important near-term signal for precious metals investors: the setup that produces the most explosive silver moves is precisely the one where the metal has already broken out technically while speculative positioning remains at or near its lows, as short-covering and fresh long-building compound each other's impact. At sub-10,000 managed money net long contracts in silver, the market is structurally coiled for a positioning squeeze on any continuation of the metals' upside.

headline: WHERE EXPERTS SEE GOLD AND SILVER GOING IN AUGUST — STRUCTURAL SILVER DEFICIT ENTERS YEAR 5 AS CHINA DEMAND ACCELERATES
snippet: CBS News published an August 2026 expert roundup on gold and silver price targets that frames the current precious metals environment within a multi-year structural supply deficit thesis for silver — now in its fifth consecutive year of annual consumption exceeding mine supply — and a gold bull market supported by persistent central bank accumulation, de-dollarisation flows from Asian investors, and a US labour market that, per the July NFP data, is now weakening faster than the Federal Reserve anticipated heading into the election cycle. Expert consensus for gold in August 2026 broadly targets $4,400–$4,700, with a path toward the January 2026 all-time high of $5,598 re-opening if inflation data remains tame and the Fed holds rates through autumn. Silver's expert range centres on $65–$75 for August, with at least one analyst projecting triple-digit silver by year-end — a target predicated on the gold-silver ratio compressing from its current level near 67x toward the 30–40x range historically seen at precious metals cycle peaks. The structural underpinning for silver is industrial: solar panel manufacturing (20% of annual silver demand), EV electrical systems, and AI data centre power infrastructure are all growing faster than analysts projected 18 months ago. China's silver imports in the first two months of 2026 hit an eight-year high at over 790 tonnes — driven by both solar manufacturing front-loading ahead of export tax rebate changes and retail investor demand as Chinese savers continued shifting from property into hard assets.
